To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a transcription-factor protein of the LRP/ASN family from the hyperthermoarchaeon Pyrococcus OT3 has been crystallized and that the structure of the protein has been determined to 3.0-A resolution.
we have determined the crystal structure of a protein from a hyperthermoarchaeal species, Pyrococcus sp OT3.
we have determined the secondary structure of a protein belonging to the family of the Lrp and AsnC transcription factors, which are involved in the control of a number of metabolic pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the structure determination of the Lrp family of transcription factors, which are involved in the regulation of the transcription of genes involved in amino acid metabolism in E. coli and in other bacteria.
the structure determination of the protein pot1216151.
the structural characterization of pot121615, which belongs to a new family of transcription regulators.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Lrp/AscC protein family is highly conserved among the hyperthermophiles.
pot1216151 has a similar fold to the Lrp family of proteins, and it is the first protein from the AsnC/Lrp family to be determined from a hyperthermo-philic archaeon.
the Lrp/AscN transcription-factor family may be a good target for the discovery of new thermostable enzymes and for the design of novel biotechnology processes.
